% Fixture reproducing the structure of the widely used "Jake's Resume" template,
% which is what the real master resume is built on. It exists to pin down four
% bugs that only this shape of document exposes:
%
%   1. \newcommand definitions in the preamble contain a literal \item, which a
%      naive scan offers up as a droppable bullet — trimming one would destroy
%      the document.
%   2. \resumeProjectHeading nests \textbf{\href{..}{\underline{Name}}}, so an
%      entry-label regex without brace matching never finds the project name.
%   3. A "% ---- Section ----" comment sits between the summary text and the next
%      \section, so a span running to the next section swallows it and escaping
%      turns the comment into printed text.
%   4. \input{glyphtounicode} and \pdfgentounicode are pdfTeX-only and abort
%      XeTeX, which is the engine Tectonic runs.
\documentclass[letterpaper,10pt]{article}
\usepackage[margin=0.4in]{geometry}
\usepackage{titlesec}
\usepackage{enumitem}
\usepackage[hidelinks]{hyperref}
\input{glyphtounicode}
\pdfgentounicode=1

\titleformat{\section}{\vspace{-2pt}\scshape\raggedright\large}{}{0em}{}[\titlerule \vspace{-6pt}]

\newcommand{\resumeItem}[1]{
    \item\small{#1 \vspace{-2pt}}
}

\newcommand{\resumeSubheading}[4]{
    \vspace{-2pt}\item
    \begin{tabular*}{0.97\textwidth}[t]{l@{\extracolsep{\fill}}r}
        \textbf{#1} & #2 \\
        \textit{\small #3} & \textit{\small #4} \\
    \end{tabular*}\vspace{-7pt}
}

\newcommand{\resumeProjectHeading}[2]{
    \item
    \begin{tabular*}{0.97\textwidth}{l@{\extracolsep{\fill}}r}
        \small #1 & #2 \\
    \end{tabular*}\vspace{-7pt}
}

\newcommand{\resumeItemListStart}{\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=0.18in]}
\newcommand{\resumeItemListEnd}{\end{itemize}\vspace{-6pt}}

\begin{document}
